David / team / Evan —

Quick engineering note and recommended configuration (summary first, details below):

Recommendation (three-tier):
- Option A — Conserved (low risk): 2x a100-40GB per region reserved (min 8 GPUs US-east, min 8 GPUs US-west) with autoscale pool to add 6 GPUs per region for burst (24-month term qualifies for 12% discount).
- Option B — Balanced (recommended): mixed fleet (a100-80GB + h100-80GB) with min guarantee 16 GPUs per region (32 total), burst pool +50% (managed warm-standby) for up to 4 hours/day. Includes KV prefix caching per region and prewarming window (2 hours) before launch events.
- Option C — Aggressive (performance-first): 48 GPUs per region (96 total), hot-standby lanes and priority routing (SLA-backed). Best for sustained high-throughput generative workloads.

Engineering detail:
- Region semantics: min guarantees are enforced per-region. We’ll map two isolated GPU pools (us-east-1, us-west-2) with dedicated control-plane routing so traffic remains local.
- Burst behavior: burst capacity is drawn from a shared flexible pool (customer-dedicated tranche) with pre-allocated warm-standby instances. For same-day launches we require a 2-hour prewarm trigger (we can automate this via webhook from your CI/CD or calendar invite); for ad-hoc spikes we have a fast-path request that targets +50% for up to 4 hours, subject to capacity availability and with fallback to model-variants if needed. We can include a runway credit (first two same-day bursts per quarter guaranteed).
- KV cache and latency: allocate KV cache shards per region to keep tail latency within target (<60ms). For Balanced we recommend model quantization to int8 where appropriate to reduce token latency.
- Warm-up and onboarding: 2 weeks of joint runbook and 40 hours of Redwood PS to tune batching and routing prior to GA.

I’ll attach a simple capacity table if helpful (I’ve included in the shared Drive link). Happy to jump on a 30-min sizing call with Evan and Priya.

—Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options + sample ramp (Luminexa) — consolidated proposal

Evan / Priya —

Thanks for the clarifying questions and for the call earlier today. Based on your target launch windows and the sample traffic, here are consolidated, actionable options. We kept them explicit so procurement can compare TCO quickly.

Option 1 — Conservative (lower up-front)
- Architecture: 2 isolated regions (us-east-1, us-west-2)
- Min guarantee: 8 GPUs / region (total 16) — a100-40GB baseline
- Burst: +50% available from customer tranche; same-day bursts require 2-hour prewarm request, two guaranteed same-day bursts per quarter
- Term & pricing: 12 months; baseline price X, 24-month discount not applied
- Onboarding: 2 weeks, 20 PS hours

Option 2 — Balanced (recommended)
- Architecture: regional isolation with mixed fleet
- Min guarantee: 16 GPUs / region (total 32) — a100-80GB + h100 mix
- Burst: +50% hot-standby lanes with automated prewarm (webhook) and 4 hours/day headroom for launches
- Term & pricing: 12 months default; 24-month term = additional 12% discount (applied to committed spend)
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for reserved lanes; same-day capacity augmentation best-effort with runway credits (first 2/quarter guaranteed)
- Onboarding: 2-week runbook + 40 PS hours for tuning

Option 3 — Performance (sustained/high throughput)
- Architecture: regional isolation + hot standby
- Min guarantee: 48 GPUs / region (96 total)
- Burst: dedicated hot-standby; immediate capacity for planned launches
- Term & pricing: 24 months recommended; pricing tiered with enterprise add-ons
- Onboarding: 4-week program + 120 PS hours

Next steps: please indicate which option you prefer (1/2/3), whether you want a 12- or 24-month term, and any procurement constraints. If you’re ready, Laura can assemble a redline-ready SOW and price appendix.

If useful I can schedule a 30-min call with Karthik to walk through the burst/launch runbook.

Cheers,
David
David Kim
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
